resource_no_psutil: psutil not installed: Pause/Resume, live CPU-core control, and CPU/GPU stats are unavailable. Install with: pip install psutil (then restart this app).
note_cores_priority: Cores and priority apply at Start, and live while running.
note_pro_mode: Full CRF range, extra tone-mapping curves, brightness trim.
note_resolution: Width is computed automatically to keep the source's aspect ratio.
container_note: MP4 — widest device/player support. MKV — needed if the source has subtitle or audio tracks (e.g. PGS, DTS) that MP4 can't hold when copied as-is.
note_setup: Installs FFmpeg and/or HandBrakeCLI via winget if missing. Progress streams into Activity. Windows may show a permission (UAC) prompt during install — that's normal.
tonemap_info_bt.2390: The reference curve most professional HDR-to-SDR grades are built around. Good default - balances highlight rolloff and midtone contrast without extra setup. Needs a Vulkan GPU.
tonemap_info_hable: A filmic curve (originally from Uncharted 2) - smooth highlight rolloff, punchy midtones. Solid default when BT.2390 isn't available, and the default HandBrake also uses internally.
tonemap_info_reinhard: Simple and fast, but tends to look flatter/lower-contrast than Hable or BT.2390 - a reasonable fallback, not usually the first choice.
tonemap_info_mobius: Similar territory to Hable with a gentler shoulder into highlights - can hold onto slightly more detail in bright areas at the cost of a flatter overall look.
tonemap_info_bt.2446a: ITU's method aimed at broadcast/TV mastering conventions rather than BT.2390's cinema-leaning target - worth trying if BT.2390 looks a bit too contrasty for your source.
tonemap_info_auto: Lets libplacebo pick per-scene rather than applying one fixed curve throughout. Can adapt better to sources with wildly inconsistent brightness, at the cost of predictability.
tonemap_info_st2094-40: Uses the source's own HDR10+ dynamic metadata if present - most accurate option when that metadata actually exists, but does nothing extra on a plain HDR10 source that lacks it.
tonemap_info_st2094-10: Same idea as ST2094-40 but for the less common ST2094-10 metadata standard - only useful if your source actually carries it.
tonemap_info_linear: No highlight rolloff at all - bright areas clip hard rather than compress gracefully. Mainly useful for testing/comparison, rarely what you want for a final export.
tonemap_info_gamma: A flat power-curve remap rather than a perceptual tone-mapping curve - simple, but doesn't handle extreme highlights as gracefully as Hable/BT.2390.
tonemap_info_clip: Hard-clips anything above SDR white instead of compressing it - fast, but loses all detail in blown-out highlights. Mostly a diagnostic/testing option.
tonemap_info_none: Passes values through with no tone mapping at all - output will look washed out or broken on an SDR display. Only useful for troubleshooting the pipeline itself.

analysis_note_dolby: Dolby Vision detected. A compatible HDR10 base layer is required for dependable SDR output.
analysis_note_hdr: HDR detected. Tone mapping is appropriate.
analysis_note_sdr: Likely SDR/Rec.709. Tone mapping is normally unnecessary.
analysis_failed_unicode: Analysis failed reading ffprobe's output ({error}). This is usually a corrupted/unusual metadata tag in the file itself, not a problem with the video streams - conversion can often still proceed.
rec_sdr: Tone mapping isn't really needed here - if you convert anyway, a gentle CPU tonemap curve (or Pro mode → None) is safer than forcing BT.2390 on non-HDR footage.
rec_dolby: Results depend on this file having a usable HDR10 base layer - if the output looks off, that's the likely reason.
rec_hdr10plus: This source carries HDR10+ dynamic metadata - enable Pro mode and pick ST2094-40 for the most accurate result.
rec_bt2390_good: BT.2390 on GPU (the default) is a good fit for this source.
rec_no_bt2390: This FFmpeg build has no usable BT.2390/libplacebo - Hable (CPU tonemap) is the best curve available here.
dlg_already_running_msg: A conversion is already in progress.
dlg_setup_in_progress_msg: Wait for dependency installation to finish first.
dlg_handbrake_missing_msg: Install HandBrakeCLI and ensure it's on PATH, or switch the backend to FFmpeg.
dlg_already_sdr_msg: This source appears to be SDR; conversion was not started.
dlg_dolby_question: Continue only if it contains an HDR10-compatible base layer?

tooltip_preset_best: Apply the Best quality settings: CPU · H.265, Pro mode, low CRF, best available curve. Slower.

tooltip_save_frame: Save frame — save the current preview frame to disk as an image.

tooltip_test_clip_open_initial: Open test clip — no test clip rendered yet. Turns green once one is ready to play.
tooltip_test_clip_cancel: Cancel the test clip render currently in progress.

preset_optimal_note_sdr: tone mapping off — already the default for non-HDR sources
preset_optimal_note_dolby: BT.2390 · GPU, same as HDR — needs a usable HDR10 base layer
preset_optimal_note_hdr10plus: ST2094-40 · Pro mode — matches this source's HDR10+ metadata
preset_optimal_note_bt2390: BT.2390 · GPU — already the app default
preset_optimal_note_fallback: Hable · CPU — BT.2390/libplacebo unavailable in this FFmpeg build
preset_best_note: CPU · H.265, Pro mode, low CRF — slower, highest fidelity
preset_fast_note_gpu: {gpu} — hardware, much faster, still solid quality
preset_fast_note_cpu: CPU · H.264 or a higher CRF — no hardware encoder detected ({cores} cores)
perf_rec_gpu: For speed with still-solid quality, this machine has {gpu} available — much faster than CPU encoding. For the best achievable quality (at the cost of encode time), use CPU · H.265 with Pro mode and a low CRF instead.
perf_rec_cpu: No hardware encoder was detected here, so encoding runs on the CPU ({cores} cores available) — CPU · H.265 gives the best quality; CPU · H.264, a higher CRF, or limiting cores less aggressively trades some quality for shorter encode times.
